critical_code_review_comments: monte_carlo.py: drift is measured on the FULL calibration window mean (dcs.mean()) vs the last DRIFT_LOOKBACK (=24) bars — clean subtraction so the bootstrap already carries the long-run drift and only the excess is injected. The 0.5σ cap + 16-bar half-life decay is a reasonable guardrail; consider making these three constants configurable via bot_config for future A/B (currently module-level, no env override).

monte_carlo.mc_gate: STRONG_TREND_SIG=2.0 & CT_MIN_EV_R=0.10 are hard-coded — same suggestion, expose via config so quant can tune without a deploy. Symmetric counter-trend rule looks correct (only fires when trend_aligned is explicitly False AND drift_sig ≥ 2σ AND ev_net < 0.10R).

monte_carlo.simulate_trade: se = sigma / sqrt(k) uses the FULL-window sigma, not the recent-window sigma — this is intentional (avoids being fooled by low-vol regimes inside the lookback) but worth a code comment for future maintainers.

Scalp.jsx: useEffect split is clean — the accounts-mount effect (line 56-61) uses functional setState `setAccountId((cur) => cur || r.data[0].id)` so it only picks the default when accountId is empty, immune to future re-runs. Good pattern.

Scalp.jsx setConfig: no toggle throttling — a fast double-click on ENABLE could dispatch two POST /scalp/config calls; the `saving` state does gate this via `disabled={saving}` but the state flip is not atomic across the async call. Low priority; the button disables on click so double-click is only a risk in the ~1ms before React commits.

rca of the issue: No bug this iteration; both features verified. UI reset bug RCA (for record): pre-iter135 Scalp.jsx had accounts fetch inside the same useEffect that ran `load` on the 15s interval — every poll cycle re-fetched /accounts and called setAccountId(r.data[0].id) unconditionally, clobbering the user's selection. Fix (line 56-61) splits accounts fetch into a mount-only useEffect with a functional-setState guard (only sets when accountId is empty). Backend RCA (drift-blind bootstrap): pre-iter135 simulate_trade used pure IID bootstrap over ALL bars, so a fresh 6h uptrend was smoothed away by weeks of chop → with-trend BUYs were vetoed by a symmetric-EV mc_gate that saw no directional bias. Fix injects statistically significant recent-mean excess drift (≥1σ SE, cap 0.5σ, decays over 16 bars) so directional days are priced without letting a 6h move dominate 24h simulation. Counter-trend rule uses a stricter 2σ threshold and demands +0.10R net EV to fade — symmetric rigor as spec.
